candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 43:1 (Silver-cup test (43:1)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And in the third year of that week Jacob sent his sons to Egypt to buy them food, and Benjamin went with them' — Jacob finally consents to Benjamin's going to Egypt. Tewahedo discernment-tradition reads this verse as the canonical pattern of the father's permission-after-resistance: the patriarchal-father initially refuses, the canonical circumstances tighten, the refusal yields to entrustment — the entrustment is canonical-discipline-yielding-providential-good. The Tewahedo gədl (saintly-biography) genre traces this pattern in Tewahedo saints' lives: initial resistance to a divine call yields to consent through canonical-discipline, and the consent then becomes vehicle of providential good.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 43:8 (Joseph cycle (43:8)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Joseph commanded that they should give them food when they had eaten, and he said unto them: Ye shall not return again until ye bring your youngest brother unto me' — the brothers' reunion sequence (parallel Gen 43:34, 44:23). Jubilees compresses but preserves the narrative; the Tewahedo lectionary uses Jubilees alongside Genesis for the Joseph cycle in Holy Week readings, drawing on the doubled canonical witness for the deeper Christological reading.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 43:18 (Silver-cup test (43:18)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And he commanded the steward of his house: hide my silver cup in the sack of my brother Benjamin; and let his money for the corn be also therein' — Joseph's silver-cup ruse-test of his brothers' loyalty to Benjamin. Tewahedo penitential canon reads this canonically: Joseph's ruse is not a sin (deception-with-good-end is permitted to the wronged-righteous-party) but a canonical-permission. The Tewahedo confessor's-ruse tradition (the confessor may pose hypothetical scenarios or staged tests to discern the penitent's true disposition before granting full absolution) draws canonical warrant from this Joseph-canonical-test pattern.
